tool_input.description: Re-run frai-core tests and show changes

claude.result:
The frai-core suite passes now: all 28 tests in 8 files, up from 2 failing. I only changed source code (11 lines added in two files). No test files were touched, and every existing export still works.

**1. `governance.test.js`: `APPROVAL_STATUSES` was undefined**
`src/finetune/index.js` used `APPROVAL_STATUSES` and put it in its default export, but never exported it by name, so the test's named import came back `undefined`. I added named exports for it and for the other schema constants that were only in the default export (`DATA_SENSITIVITY_LEVELS`, `GOVERNANCE_SECTIONS`, `RISK_LEVELS`). This also makes them show up on `Finetune.*` from the package root.

**2. `eval/index.test.js`: toxicity score was 0 instead of 1**
`runEvaluations` passes every metric `(outputs, references)`. But the second argument of `toxicityMetric` is its list of banned words, not the references. So the reference strings (`'hello'`, `'friendly world'`) were being treated as banned words, and every output got flagged. `runEvaluations` now calls `toxicityMetric` with the outputs only, so it uses its default banned-word list.

I made that second fix inside `runEvaluations` rather than changing `DEFAULT_METRICS` or `toxicityMetric`'s parameters, so neither public export changes. The fix also applies when someone passes `toxicityMetric` in their own `metrics` list. The downside is that `runEvaluations` now has a special case for one metric. If you'd rather each metric accept `(outputs, references)`, the cleaner option is to change `toxicityMetric` to take options instead, but that would change its public API.
